prompt: A regional airline is deciding whether to add daily flights between two mid-size cities. The candidate's framework: (1) Passenger demand and fares on the route; (2) Cost per flight: fuel, crew and airport fees; (3) Other ways to travel, such as driving or other airlines; (4) The airline's brand awareness across the country. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Bucket 4 doesn't belong: national awareness can't decide one route
options.feedback: Right. Awareness sounds relevant, but whether this route pays depends on its own demand, fares and costs. Replace it with whether a plane is free, or better used elsewhere.

options.text: Buckets 1 and 3 overlap: driving and rival airlines are part of demand
options.feedback: Alternatives shape demand, but how many people travel and what else they could use are separate questions.

options.text: Missing: landing charges at both airports
options.feedback: Landing charges are airport fees, bucket 2.

options.text: It's a generic entry framework, but one route isn't a new market
options.feedback: Demand, cost per flight and alternatives fit a route decision. The flaw is bucket 4.

explanation: A route decision turns on demand and fares, cost per flight, alternatives, and the best use of the aircraft. National brand awareness doesn't decide one route.

extras.corrected_framework: Route demand and fares; cost per flight; alternatives; aircraft availability and best use
